title: On with singular owners
focus: Use fixed on with minulla, sinulla, and hänellä to say what the owner has.

exercises.prompt: Choose “I have a book.” in Finnish. Use minulla (“I as the owner”) and kirja (“a book”). Frame: “Minulla ___ kirja”.
exercises.explanation: Minulla names the owner. This possession pattern uses fixed on to say what that owner has.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Fixed on in possession: form or meaning confused

Minulla names the owner. This possession pattern uses fixed on to say what that owner has.
Minulla names the owner. This possession pattern uses fixed on to say what that owner has. This choice uses the wrong verb form.
This choice changes the required polarity or leaves the required question pattern.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: possessor + fixed on + one thing in its basic singular form

parts.role: possessor: the person who has the thing
parts.formation: minä has the learned possession form minulla; its -lla/-llä ending marks the possessor. Learn this pronoun form as a whole.
Olla means “to be”; possession uses fixed on with minulla, sinulla and hänellä.
kirja stays in its basic singular form: one book.

answerDiagnostics.category: Fixed on in possession: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: The -lla/-llä phrase is the possessor. In this possession pattern the verb stays fixed, so do not conjugate it to match the owner.
